correctness.rationale: Asgarli–Duan–Lai Theorem 1.6(3) independently supplies the exhaustive normalized form F0+G(X²,Y²,Z²); the Jacobian partials of F0 are exactly the F4 Frobenius collinearity equations, whose geometric zero locus is the 21 F4 projective points. Two standalone independently written implementations enumerate all 4^10 normalized coefficient vectors and agree that exactly 960 avoid all 21 points. An independent C++ full-group enumeration of 181,440 invertible 3x3 matrices finds exactly 189 stabilizing the explicit representative (with rank-10 interpolation), giving the same 960 orbit; additionally, a verified affine coefficient action of eight F4-projective maps preserves the full smooth set, and exact BFS from the minimum vector reaches all 960, proving transitivity; 60480/960=63. The representative also admits a direct nonvanishing argument. Exact arithmetic is finite and exhaustive, with no extrapolation from samples.

originality.rationale: The literature already gives the complete coefficient-family normal form and one explicit F4 sextic (ADL, Thm 1.6 and Ex 4.11), not the 960 smooth coefficient count or single PGL3(F4) orbit. Borges–Korchmáros–Speziali Thm 4.21 classifies curves invariant under a stipulated Singer-normalizer subgroup up to projectivity over F_{4^3}; it neither establishes that all smooth extremal Frobenius-nonclassical F4-sextics possess that symmetry nor their precise F4-rational projective equivalence and number of models. Targeted mathematical-record and literature alias/parameter searches, and accessible earlier published claims, did not yield a dominating result. The result remains a same-model novelty assessment, not a proof of historical nonexistence.
residual_risks: An older or poorly indexed result on Singer-normalizer/Pellikaan models might imply the same F4-rational orbit without naming Frobenius nonclassicality.
The orbit computation is finite exhaustive code and algebraic reasoning, but no independent formal or external audit has been performed.
The known classification under extension-field projectivity is close to, but not equivalent to, the present rational-field rigidity; further expert priority review would help.

The Cossidente–Siciliano 2003 Singer-automorphism classification is accessible only in abstract/secondary form here; its precise finite-field hypotheses remain a priority-review gap, although the accessible 2022 source confirms a conditional extension-field statement rather than universal rational-field transitivity.

value.rationale: The principal source characterizes an entire maximal-degree exceptional class but exhibits only isolated explicit examples. Determining that all 960 smooth F4 normalized models fall into one rational projective orbit is a natural complete moduli/rigidity classification in the smallest nonprime binary field, not an arbitrary slice or a textbook consequence. The explicit diagonal representative and sharp 63-element rational stabilizer make the structure reusable for subsequent arithmetic and group-action calculations. The scope is finite but exhaustive and mathematically motivated; it claims neither broader-field results nor any independent validation.
